name: music_saves_videos
summary: An educational video essay examining the impact of popular needle drops on film and content editing. It features fast-paced pacing with frequent timeline screen captures, reaction picture-in-picture windows, and beat-matched audio-visual demos.

captions.notes: No continuous spoken dialogue captions; only sporadic graphic titles and source film subtitles appear.

headline.notes: Bold, centered uppercase text pops on screen to introduce key concepts and topic chapters.

callouts.notes: Minimalist onscreen labels and arrows highlight timeline details and UI elements.

transitions.notes: Dominated by hard cuts with frequent audio J/L cuts to preview music cues before visual cuts.

rules: Cut to timeline or NLE playback within 3 seconds of introducing an editing problem.
Punch in on the A-roll speaker to emphasize strong emotional reactions.
Place speaker reaction cam in a picture-in-picture corner during full-screen playback.
Sync visual impacts and cut points directly to musical beat drops.
Use J-cuts to lead into music transitions ahead of video clips.
Punch in to closer focal length on punchy remarks or comedic beats
Display editing timeline beneath playback footage to show technical process
Nest creator webcam reaction in top corner during playback tests
Cut video previews sharply to music beats and audio stingers
Use clean screen capture showing cursor navigation for software and web demos
Keep talking head background softly blurred with colored rim lighting
Emphasize key takeaways with bold, white, centered uppercase typography
avoid: No full-length burned-in animated karaoke subtitles.
No decorative stock transitions like light leaks or whip zooms.
No static shots longer than 6 seconds without a camera punch or cutaway.
No unmotivated background music during audio comparison segments.
Aggressive whip pans or flashy distortion transitions
Loud sound effect whooshes on every graphic element
Static wide shots longer than 6 seconds without a camera reframing
